patch.lastPrompt: You are an expert C++ to Rust migration engineer. Read the following C++ source code: --- Source (/workspace/dataset/color/tests/test13.cpp) --- #include "../color.hpp" #include <iostream> using namespace ColorSpace; int main(int argc, char* argv[]) { float h1 = 30.0f, s1 = 0.6f, l1 = 0.5f; float h2 = 210.0f, s2 = 0.4f, l2 = 0.7f; if (argc > 5) { h1 = std::stof(argv[1]); s1 = std::stof(argv[2]); l1 = std::stof(argv[3]); h2 = std::stof(argv[4]); s2 = std::stof(argv[5]); } if (argc > 6) { l2 = std::stof(argv[6]); } HSL hsl1(h1, s1, l1); HSL hsl2(h2, s2, l2); float hueDiff = ColorConverter::hueDifference(hsl1, hsl2); std::cout << hueDiff << std::endl; return 0; } /* ============================== TEST CASE EXAMPLES (Top 5) ============================== --- Example 1 --- Input Args: {"h1": "0", "s1": "0", "l1": "0", "h2": "360", "s2": "1", "l2": "1"} Program Output: 0 --- Example 2 --- Input Args: {"h1": "180", "s1": "0.5", "l1": "0.5", "h2": "180", "s2": "0.5", "l2": "0.5"} Program Output: 0 --- Example 3 --- Input Args: {"h1": "0", "s1": "0.5", "l1": "0.5", "h2": "180", "s2": "0.5", "l2": "0.5"} Program Output: 180 --- Example 4 --- Input Args: {"h1": "90", "s1": "1", "l1": "0.5", "h2": "270", "s2": "1", "l2": "0.5"} Program Output: 180 --- Example 5 --- Input Args: {"h1": "45", "s1": "0.25", "l1": "0.75", "h2": "225", "s2": "0.25", "l2": "0.75"} Program Output: 180 */ --- Requirements: 1. **Environment**: Write pure Rust using the 2021 edition. Code must compile with `rustc` or as a Cargo project. 2. **CLI arguments**: The Rust binary must accept exactly the same command-line arguments as the C++ binary (same names, defaults, and required fields). Parse args via `std::env::args()`. 3. **Logic and output**: Algorithm logic, numeric precision, and string formatting must exactly match the C++ source. `println!` output must be byte-for-byte identical to `std::cout` output. 4. **Zero external dependencies**: Do NOT use any crates from crates.io (only `std`). Forbidden crates for this repo: none. Implement all functionality from scratch using the standard library. 5. **Project structure**: Create a complete Cargo project in `/output`. Organize library code into modules. Place the entry test file `test13.rs` in the package root `/output`. 6. **Black-box implementation**: Do not read the C++ library source. Infer behavior from the interface, then re-implement using `std`. 7. **Output**: - Create and implement library files inside `/output`. - Save the entry file to `/output/test13.rs`. - Compile and produce an executable at `/output/test13.rs` (by running `rustc test13.rs` or `cargo build --release`). Hint: `/workspace/dataset/test13_executable` is the compiled C++ binary — use it to debug with any arguments.

args.command: cd /output && cargo build --release 2>&1 | tail -3 && rustc --edition 2021 test13.rs -o /tmp/test13_rustc 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "builds done"

display.command: cd /output && cargo build --release 2>&1 | tail -3 && rustc --edition 2021 test13.rs -o /tmp/test13_rustc 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "builds done"

args.command:
cd /output
REF=/workspace/dataset/test13_executable
BIN=target/release/test13
fail=0
check() {
  a=$($REF "$@"); b=$($BIN "$@")
  if [ "$a" != "$b" ]; then echo "MISMATCH args=[$*] ref=[$a] rust=[$b]"; fail=1; fi
}
# 5 documented examples
check 0 0 0 360 1 1
check 180 0.5 0.5 180 0.5 0.5
check 0 0.5 0.5 180 0.5 0.5
check 90 1 0.5 270 1 0.5
check 45 0.25 0.75 225 0.25 0.75
# probed edge cases
check 10 0.5 0.5 350 0.5 0.5
check 720 0.5 0.5 0 0.5 0.5
check 400 0.5 0.5 40 0.5 0.5
check -30 0.5 0.5 30 0.5 0.5
check 10000000 0.5 0.5 0 0.5 0.5
check 0.00001 0.5 0.5 0 0.5 0.5
check 45.123456789 0.5 0.5 0 0.5 0.5
check 33.333333 0.5 0.5 0 0.5 0.5
check 0.1 0.5 0.5 0.2 0.5 0.5
check 180.5 0.5 0.5 0 0.5 0.5
# default / partial args
check
check 1 2 3 4 5
check 1 2 3 4 5 6
check 100 0.5 0.5 260 0.9 0.1 0.3
# fuzz
for i in $(seq 1 300); do
  check "$(awk 'BEGIN{srand('$i'); printf "%.7g %.7g %.7g %.7g %.7g %.7g", (rand()-0.5)*2000, rand(), rand(), (rand()-0.5)*2000, rand(), rand()}')"
done
for i in $(seq 301 400); do
  check "$(awk 'BEGIN{srand('$i'); printf "%.10g 0.5 0.5 %.10g 0.5 0.5", (rand()-0.5)*1e8, (rand()-0.5)*1e-3}')"
done
[ $fail -eq 0 ] && echo "ALL MATCH"
